_comment: The rooms between the arenas: what stands in one, and which three doors it
offers on the way out. game/rooms.py holds the arithmetic and none of the
values, the way game/loot.py and game/progression.py do.
*** enabled: false IS THE ROLLBACK. ***
Switched off, no reward room is ever built, a cleared arena leads straight
to the next one, and scenes/play.py puts the shop back on every transition
-- which is the game exactly as it was measured. The code goes quiet
without being removed, the same switch gold.base and xp_base already are.
NOTHING BELOW IS MEASURED, AND THE REASON IS DELIBERATE. The reference bot
walks from a room's entrance to a door and touches nothing on the way. So
no fixture in this file moves any bracket, and the campaign the harness
measures is arithmetically the campaign it measured before rooms existed.
That was not the first draft. The bot used to walk to the fixture and use
it, and three of the four rewards were inert to it anyway -- it never buys
at a stall, never spends a shrine's point, never spends a chest's gold. The
fountain was the exception, and over twelve seeds it flipped one entire run
from won to lost. The trace is the interesting part: the losing run arrived
at the stage it died on with MORE health than the surviving one. The heal
moved the hero a little further along on stage 15 and forty stages of a
deterministic fight amplified it. That is the measurement reporting its own
perturbation, in the same units it reports difficulty -- which is the exact
trap data/entities.json records against the flanker demon.
So the numbers below are guesses in the strongest sense: not 'unverified',
but 'nothing in the suite can see them at all'. Treat every one as an
opening bid, and change them with hands on a keyboard rather than with
tools/balance.py, which is structurally incapable of having an opinion.
_doors_comment: Three distinct kinds, never three of the same. Duplicates would be cheaper
to roll and would read as a bug at 16px -- two identical icons on one wall
look like the room forgot to decide rather than like a repeated option.
The doors do not all sit on one wall any more. They stand on the three
walls the hero did NOT come in through, ordered left, forward, right -- so
the door taken decides which wall the next room is entered by, and the room
turns with the run. See tools/make_rooms.py for the geometry and
game/rooms.DOOR_ORDER for why forward is the middle one.
Three doors against three kinds outside the stall, so off a stall floor
every offer holds all three and only the order moves. That is a real cost:
the old 'four kinds, three doors, one always missing' tension now survives
only on the stall floors. Drop this to 2 to get it back everywhere.
_stall_every_comment: The stall stands on every Nth floor and on no other. It is a schedule, not
a roll: off these floors a shop is not reachable at all, and on one it is
certain. Floors 5, 10, 15 ... 40 at N=5, of which seven are reachable --
the fortieth arena is the last thing in the run and is not followed by a
This replaced a draw-and-guarantee pair (three of four kinds every
transition, plus 'a shop within four if none turned up'). The two cannot
both hold, and the schedule is the better half: gold that can never be
spent is not a reward, and now the player knows exactly how far the next
chance to spend it is rather than trusting one will turn up.
The stall goes on the LAST door, never the first. See the note in
game/rooms.offer: door 0 is the one anything mechanical reaches for.
0 switches the stall off entirely -- no door anywhere leads to one, which
is the rollback above 'stall.offers: 0' below. 1 puts one on every floor.
UNMEASURED, like every number in this file. Seven shops across a run that
banks ~24,500g, against 2,060g to max the permanents, pushes on the
late-run surplus docs/limits.md already records -- and autoplay never
spends, so nothing here can tell you whether it pushed too hard.
_first_comment: The room after arena 1 was never chosen -- there was no door before it --
so it is fixed. A fountain, because it is the gentlest of the four and
because the one room every player is guaranteed to see is the right place
for the mechanic to explain itself.
_reward_comment: Four first-pass guesses, drafted against the recorded shape of the game.
fountain.heal_percent 15 -- percent of MAXIMUM health, not of missing.
Percent rather than flat so it means the same thing to a 130-hp
Knight and a 70-hp Rogue. Of maximum rather than of missing because a
fraction-of-missing heal pays the nearly-dead most, and free healing
for a hero who refuses to disengage is precisely what the face-tank
ceiling exists to refuse.
For scale: heal_between_stages is already 56 of a Knight's 130 (43%)
on every transition, so this is about a third again on the
transitions it lands, not a new source of healing on its own.
stall.offers 3 -- how many rolled pieces of gear sit above the five
consumables. The pieces themselves are data/equipment.json; this is
only how many of them a shelf shows. Three because that is the number
of doors, and a room that offers three of everything reads as one
decision repeated rather than two unrelated ones.
SET IT TO 0 AND THE STALL IS THE SHOP EXACTLY AS IT WAS -- the five
goods and nothing above them. That is the narrow rollback for the
gear layer, underneath the whole-layer 'enabled: false' above.
shrine.offers 3 -- how many of the eight attributes a shrine puts on its
plinth, drawn distinct from its own stateless stream. Three of eight
rather than all eight, so a point is a decision about what is in
front of you rather than a menu that is the same at every shrine.
SET IT TO 8 AND EVERY SHRINE OFFERS EVERYTHING, which is the shrine
exactly as it was. Above 8 is refused by progression.offers.
shrine.points 1 -- one point, the same unit progression.json pays per
level. It is the ONLY route to the attribute layer in the shipped
game: xp_base is 0, so no kill ever pays a level and the panel would
otherwise never open. Note what that buys -- the attributes become
reachable without experience being turned on, and turning experience
on is the half that would move the recorded grid.
treasure.gold 40 with floor_step 0.15 -- the same depth curve the kill
payout uses (loot.json), for the same reason: a chest on floor 40
should be worth what floor 40 is worth. 40 is a little over a stage
of ordinary early income and a fraction of a late one, so a chest is
a nudge early and a rounding error late. That asymmetry is probably
wrong and is the first thing to look at once anyone has played it.
